object_description: long single-story school complex beneath a folding roof
design_condition: A long building is placed across the headland in the extension of the factory building, dividing the landscape into two areas while organizing gardens, courts, and sports space on either side.

positive.statement: The outdoor-space project integrates all required outdoor areas into a landscape-like design.

position.rationale: The long footprint and surrounding open areas visibly organize a broad site composition.

positive.statement: The intention to create a site-specific landscape developed from the stream-delta morphology is appreciated.

position.rationale: Landscape morphology is not directly sampled; the western open side is a plausible constrained anchor.

positive.statement: The tree population is carefully supplemented with new plantings that refer to the stream delta.

position.rationale: Plantings are not distinguishable, so the eastern landscape edge provides an approximate location.

positive.statement: The two-level access opens repeatedly into spacious meeting areas in front of the school rooms.

position.rationale: Interior access and rooms are not distinguishable; the central perimeter is the plausible meeting-zone anchor.

negative.statement: The settlement produces a rather coincidental and structurally questionable division of the landscape.

position.rationale: The elongated building visibly cuts across the site and separates areas on both sides.

negative.statement: The ramps are bottlenecks whose operational suitability is difficult to assess.

position.rationale: Ramps are not individually visible; the building access edge provides a constrained central anchor.

negative.statement: The architectural expression does not do justice to the sensitive setting and historic building structure.

position.rationale: The long exposed facade is clearly represented, though historic context is not visible in the sample.

negative.statement: The intended landscape theme is not successfully implemented beyond the level of the trees.

position.rationale: Only the broad open site is visible; the eastern perimeter approximates the criticized landscape treatment.

negative.statement: The oversized, surface-heavy square, promenade, and curved paths appear functional and lack spatial reference to the surrounding architecture.

position.rationale: Specific surfaces are not distinguishable; the southwestern open area is a plausible public-space anchor.

negative.statement: The historic main building is not sufficiently integrated into the design of the square.

position.rationale: The referenced existing building is not identifiable; the northeastern edge is a directional approximation.

negative.statement: The length of the new house divides the landscape and prevents a flowing, coherent landscape.

position.rationale: The elongated continuous footprint visibly dominates and divides the sampled landscape.

negative.statement: There are doubts about the suitability of the concept from an operational perspective.

position.rationale: The continuous building mass is visible, but operational suitability cannot be localized geometrically.
